The Frostmoon Scions celebrate the Moon-Prayer Night every year. The timing of the festival is not completely set in advance, and they usually make a rough estimate, then observe the changes in the Verdant Crests and Moon-Prayer Blossoms to guide them. On this day, the crescent moon at the top branches of the Verdant Crest turns into a full moon, and the Moon-Prayer Blossoms bloom with a special radiance.
Moon Marrow
On the Moon-Prayer Night, the Frostmoon Scions can open the sealed sanctuary and use the moon marrow — an energy core with the Moon Goddess's powers, capable of showing the true past.

After defeating the Rächer of Solnari, it seemed the danger had passed, and life in Nod-Krai had returned to normal. The Moon-Prayer Night was approaching, and with no urgent commissions for the Traveler and Paimon, they decided to complete their own tasks and wait for the festival. Worried about Columbina, who had expended too much energy during the battle with the Sinner, they went to visit her in the Silvermoon Hall. The Moon Goddess was planning to return to the true moon during the Moon-Prayer Night, when the kuuvahki reaches its peak, and as a parting gift, the Traveler invited Columbina to attend the festival with them. Since the former Harbinger had been ordered captured, she could not openly appear in Nod-Krai, so to figure out how to attend the festival discreetly and invite others, the Traveler and Paimon went to the Frostmoon Scions. On Hiisi Island, preparations were in full swing: kuuhenki were rehearsing a musical drum performance, artisans were sculpting, and others were preparing traditional sweets. After telling Lauma and Varka, who was helping with the celebration, of Columbina's decision, the Traveler and Paimon set off with the Grand Master to Nasha Town.

When the kuuvahki grew stronger due to the approach of the Moon, unusual Abyssal monsters began appearing throughout Nod-Krai, so strange that even the dragon Durin couldn't sense the Abyssal energy. When Durin and Albedo began studying them, they noticed that physical contact with them was impossible, and the monsters themselves were mirages. Records indicated that this phenomenon could occur in the days before and following Moon-Prayer Night, and then their numbers gradually diminish. Previously, this was a rather rare occurrence, and mirages did not take the form of Abyssal monsters. The odds of encountering these phantoms were similar to looking up in the night sky, seeing a shooting star, and managing to make a wish before it disappears. But on this Moon-Prayer Night, phantoms began appearing more frequently, and the phantom monsters hunted phantom humans, as if someone's last memories were coming to life. Furthermore, judging by the stories told by some human phantoms and their costumes, they lived in Hyperborea approximately six thousand years ago. Flins, Albedo, and Durin decided to study the phantoms in more detail, while the Traveler, Paimon, and Varka set off to visit the phantom spaceship Jahoda had reported. At Starsand Shoal, where the phantom had originated, they discovered that the ship had lain there for several generations, but no one had been able to cause it a scratch. When Flins, Albedo, and Durin, who had made thirty-nine unsuccessful attempts to change the phantoms' pasts, returned to the Curatorium of Secrets, the assembled party continued preparations for the festival.

When the Traveler and Paimon returned to the Silvermoon Hall to inquire of Columbina about her parting gift, she was nowhere to be found, and even the kuuhenki had vanished. When they returned the next morning, the Moon Goddess was still missing, and the flowers associated with her state had faded. Fearing for their friend's well-being, the Traveler and Paimon hurried to ask others if they had seen her, and along the way, they encountered Lauma, who was also worried about the goddess. On their way to Nasha Town, they encountered the founder of the Hexenzirkel, the witch Alice. Although she usually monitors the situation at the border of Teyvat, she was drawn to the phantoms in Nod-Krai, which were a sign that the border had been disturbed. This phenomenon was explained by the Trilunar Syzygy. When the Moon Goddesses still wielded the power of the world's laws, they divided the powers of life, death, time, and space among themselves, vowing never to gather them in a single body, in order to preserve the world's stability. When the Traveler received the Eternal Moon Marrow and returned the Iridescent Moon Marrow, along with the Frost Moon Goddess, all the powers of the Three Moons gathered in Nod-Krai, affecting the borders of Teyvat. When Alice arrived in Nod-Krai, she discovered that Columbina was not simply lost, but "disappeared," as Teyvat rejected her. While the Frostmoon Scions revered Columbina as their goddess Kuutar, and among the Fatui she was the Harbinger Damselette, she had a "rationale" of existence, but then these ties were severed. Once the "rationale" that sustained her existence disappeared, nothing held her in Teyvat anymore.

While the Frostmoon Scions revered Columbina as their goddess Kuutar, and among the Fatui she was the Harbinger Damselette, she had a "rationale" of existence, but then these ties were severed. Once the "rationale" that sustained her existence disappeared, nothing held her in Teyvat anymore. To save the Moon Goddess, her friends needed to strengthen her connection to Teyvat using Columbina's true name and find a way to break through Teyvat's false sky. To help the Traveler, Lauma, and the Moon Goddess's other friends, Alice invited her friend, the witch and angel Nicole.

When Columbina awoke from her sleep, she realized that her physical body had disappeared, leaving only the strength to maintain consciousness. Fearing that her consciousness might soon fade, the Moon Goddess decided to take one last look at this world. Previously, everyone had treated her as the Moon Goddess or the Fatui Harbinger, so in her 500 years of life, she had never seen how people truly lived, and only before her death did she have this chance. The Frostmoon Scions revealed a new side to her: they were having fun, playing, sharing candy with each other, like a true "family." Hoping to meet her friends, Columbina went to Nasha Town, where she saw two mechanics who had spoken ill of each other but still cared for each other. This reminded her of Sandrone, who had also promised to unscrew Columbina's vocal cords but remained her friend. When the Moon Goddess passed through the Traveler, who was heading off to meet Nicole, they suddenly turned around and called Columbina's name, as if sensing her. Deciding she wanted to spend her last moments with her friends, Columbina followed them.

Even after the Moon Goddesses perished in the War of Funerary Flame six thousand years ago, the Hyperboreans continued to pray to the goddesses for mercy. They built titanic structures that consumed vast amounts of kuuvahki and established a connection between Teyvat and the true Moons. Now Columbina could once again use this ritual to bypass the false sky. To discover such a "portal," Nicole suggested using phantoms to reach the Hyperboreans' six-thousand-year-old structure. While Nicole waited for suitable phantoms to appear, the Traveler, Paimon, Varka, and Lauma split up to try to find the true name of the Moon Goddess, but even the records of the Frostmoon Scions yielded nothing useful. After returning to Nasha Town, the Traveler and Paimon were joined by Varka and Wanderer, who had come to Nod-Krai to learn more about Dottore. Although the meeting with the Harbingers, Sandrone and Arlecchino, also failed to reveal Columbina's true name, Nicole sent a Seelie to inform them that the necessary portal had been found.
While Columbina's friends were busy searching for her name, Alice tasked Albedo and Durin with finding a way to change the phantoms' fates, but no matter how hard they tried, nothing happened. Wanderer, who joined them, suggested that Durin use Abyssal power to guide them. Among the phantoms, they encountered a Hyperborean searching for his daughter. Using the energy of the Abyss, Durin sealed dangerous areas so the man could not pass through, and although he was able to travel further than usual, his fate was ultimately unchanged. After numerous unsuccessful attempts, the phantom suddenly saw Albedo, Durin, and Wanderer and realized that they were the ones guiding it. After learning from them of the future civilizations founded after the War of Funerary Flame, the phantom, resigned to his fate, decided to spend his final moments searching for his daughter, even if it meant nothing. Although Albedo and Durin were unable to change the Hyperboreans' fate, Alice reported disturbances on the border of Teyvat.

When Nicole found the right Hyperborean ruins, three people capable of achieving resonance with kuuvahki were needed to open them. The simplest method was to extract a small amount of kuuvahki from the soil of Nod-Krai and inject it into the body. To test whether the candidates were suitable for such power, Nicole tested kuuvahki on them, and the Traveler and the Moonchanter, Lauma, passed the test. But since Grand Master Varka failed the test, they needed a third person. Nefer and Jahoda were unable to withstand kuuvahki power, while Ineffa, Aino, and Flins were unsuitable for the test. Then, Fatui Harbinger Arlecchino, who was capable of holding the Iridescent Moon Marrow within herself, came to their aid. For three days, the Traveler, Arlecchino, and Lauma were to stand motionless without food or water, while the others remained to monitor their condition. When the ritual was finally completed, Nicole was able to open a portal to the Hyperborean sanctuary.

Inside the ruins, the Traveler, Arlecchino, Lauma, Nicole, and Paimon encountered phantoms from Hyperborea, but none of them knew the name of the new Moon Goddess, as she had not yet been born. Some phantoms spoke of a mysterious "savior," but even Nicole didn't know whom they were referring to. When the Traveler and the others reached the place where the Hyperboreans communicated with the Moons, still unable to find the name of the Moon Goddess, Nicole suggested that Columbina might not have a true name, but that didn't mean she couldn't receive a new one. Then the Traveler, Paimon, Lauma, and Arlecchino imagined the Moon Goddess and gave her a name associated with her: Columbina. These memories imbued in the name were enough to bind the goddess to Teyvat. Leaving the ruins, everyone dispersed throughout the city shouting Columbina's name, while the Traveler hurried to the place of their first meeting, the Silvermoon Hall. By the time they arrived, the goddess had almost lost the strength to maintain consciousness, but the Traveler's memories gave her the power to regain her physical form.

After Columbina was rescued, her friends invited her to the Moon-Prayer Night celebrations. To avoid suspicion, Lauma and Nefer prepared Moon Goddess costumes for everyone, and people around them greeted them with, <color=#ffffffd9>"Welcome home, Moon Goddess."</color> The Frostmoon Scions and Nasha Town prepared decorations, treats, and various games for the celebration. All of Columbina's friends, as well as Durin, Albedo, and Wanderer, also came to the celebration.
Throughout the celebration, the Traveler and Paimon, unnoticed by Columbina, approached all their friends to ask them to draw a gift card for the Moon Goddess. When the Moon-Prayer Night arrived, and it was time to say goodbye, they all gave it to her together. For Columbina, this evening was the best gift she had ever received, and she promised to write them a message in moonlight that only her friends could read.

When the time came for Columbina to return to the Moon, she, the Traveler, Lauma, and Arlecchino returned to the Hyperborean sanctuary. Using the power of the Iridescent and Eternal Moon Marrows, as well as the power of the Frost Moon, they opened the moongate, and the Moon Goddess entered it. But instead of the Moon, she found herself trapped by the second of the Fatui Harbingers, Dottore. Columbina's friends rushed to her aid, but Dottore, having subjugated the Iridescent and Eternal Moon Marrows, stopped time, and only the Traveler was able to continue moving. Knowing that as long as she remained, the power of the Three Moons would serve Dottore, Columbina opened the moon gate and stepped into the reflection of the moon. After the Harbinger disappeared, Durin and Albedo contacted Alice to tell her what had happened. It was Dottore who caused a commotion at Teyvat's border to distract the Hexenzirkel. At first, Alice thought the border violation was caused by the Abyss, but when Durin and Albedo were able to influence the fate of the Hyperborean phantoms by creating variables, she realized the source lay within Teyvat. Dottore was able to create the necessary conditions and orchestrated everything so that the Moon Goddess's open portal led her directly to him.

When Wanderer learned of what had happened, he again found the Hyperborean phantoms and arranged for them to speak with Nicole via the Dodocommunicator. It turned out that the history they were describing was different from how Nicole remembered it. A certain "savior" had appeared in the Hyperboreans' history, one who never should've existed. He promised to create a new moon within a false sky and bring back their Moon Goddesses. The deceived people believed him and told him everything he wanted to know about the Moons. The "variables" that Dottore put in place were substantial enough that they even affected phantoms that he never met. On the Moon-Prayer Night, he turned to the knowledge he'd gained and created a "false moon," which, for Columbina's ritual, seemed more real than the Frost Moon beyond the heavens. Thus, the spell sent the Moon Goddess directly to Dottore, and he was able to use her power to seize the Moon Marrows. Although Columbina and Dottore had vanished, the goddess's friends were not about to give up, and they eventually defeated Dottore after restoring Columbina's rationale on Teyvat.

customize.text: Moon-Prayer Night

is a traditional festival celebrated by the Frostmoon Scions in honor of the birth of the Moon Goddess, Kuutar. Initially a purely religious holiday, it eventually evolved into the most popular festival in Nod-Krai, celebrated even by ordinary residents. When the Frostmoon Scions learned that their beliefs were false, the Moon-Prayer Night became more of a local custom than a celebration of the Moon Goddess. The holiday has no fixed date and depends on the movement of the Moon, as the Moon is closest to Teyvat on the Moon-Prayer Night. The Frostmoon Scions make a rough estimate and then determine the exact time by observing changes in the Verdant Crests and Moon-Prayer Blossoms. On this day, the crescent moon at the top branches of the Verdant Crest turns into a full moon, and the Moon-Prayer Blossoms bloom with a special radiance, considered a blessed omen. The Verdant Crest is a Divine Tree that appeared at the birth of the Moon Maiden five centuries ago, and is therefore considered a symbol of Kuutar. The Verdant Crests are mentioned in the ancient rituals of the Frostmoon Scions in prayers to the Ruler of Time, Istaroth, although they could not have existed at that time. These rituals were presumed to be a scribal error and preserved unaltered for the sake of textual fidelity.

One day, a special fragment of the Ancient Moon's Remnants called the Moon Marrow, possessing the power of the Goddess of the Eternal Moon, Aria, fell on Hiisi Island. This special relic allowed the true past to be revealed at the moment when kuuvahki in Nod-Krai reaches its peak, on Moon-Prayer Night. Only the Moonchanter has the right to take the Moon Marrow from its sealed sanctuary once a year. Thanks to the Moon Marrow, the Traveler was able to see their spaceship arrive in Nod-Krai long ago. Although no one had left the ship during this time, during the Cataclysm, the Traveler's twin came from outside to free them.

During Moon-Prayer Night, Teyvat's borders weaken, and the power of the real moon penetrates, causing the appearance of phantoms, incorporeal ghosts of the past that cannot be interacted with. Usually, the odds of encountering these phantoms are similar to looking up in the night sky, seeing a shooting star, and managing to make a wish before it disappears. However, during the Trilunar Syzygy, the forces of the Three Moons united in Nod-Krai: the Eternal Moon's Marrow was with the Traveler, the Iridescent Moon's Marrow — which should never have appeared in this world — had been retrieved, and the Goddess of the Frost Moon was in the flesh. Phantoms began to appear more frequently, and some took the form of the Abyssal monsters that preyed on the phantoms. Due to the Syzygy, phantoms of both the ancient Hyperboreans who lived six thousand years ago and the people of Nod-Krai during the Cataclysm five hundred years ago, and even the phantom of the Traveler's spaceship, appeared in Nod-Krai.

customize.text: Activities

Traditionally, the Frostmoon Scions would decorate their settlement, wear Moon-Prayer Blossoms, and celebrate the birth of the Moon Goddess through song and dance. They would also prepare food and handicrafts and give them as gifts to others. Over time, it became Nod-Krai's most lively festival. When the holiday spread beyond Hiisi Island to Nasha Town, people began decorating the city for the festival. After the victory over the Rächer of Solnari, when the people of Nod-Krai needed a celebration, the Frostmoon Scions, the Adventurers' Guild, and representatives of Nasha Town organized a large celebration, which brought together representatives of all factions. A total of eight stalls were set up at the celebration. In the main square, sponsored by the witch Alice, a large amusement wheel with Dodoco-shaped seats was set up, while kuuhenki played drums, and nearby, guests could make wishes. Nasha Town's square was decorated with a statue of a deer, carved by the artisans of the Frostmoon Scions.

At the Frostmoon Scions' stall, people could take a photo with an animal-shaped stand, inviting Lauma, a Rimehorn Deer, or the Traveler. The Moonchanter even invited many animals to join in on the fun. People got to choose a headpiece in the shape of various animal ears and horns, and even the Fatui Harbingers, Arlecchino and Sandrone, wore the animal ears. People could also get kuuhenki and animal-shaped balloons at the Frosmoon Scions' stall. When Columbina lost her physical body and went to observe the Frosmoon Scions' ordinary life, she saw children and even priestesses filling balloons with water and throwing them at each other. So, she wanted to play a game herself, setting an ambush on Jahoda. Boss Nefer came to Jahoda's aid, and Arlecchino joined Columbina's team.

At a stall set up by the Lightkeepers, the Ratnik, Flins, assumed the form of a lantern and distributed sugar sculptures of their spirit animals to children based on their answers to questions. After receiving Columbina's answers, Flins gave her a figurine of a kuuhenki, free-spirited creatures who love all things in Nod-Krai and selflessly help people. Since the Traveler and Flins had known each other for a long time, the Ratnik gave them the lantern sculpture as a sign of friendship. At the Frostmoon Scions, Columbina saw the children sharing food, so she offered the Traveler a chance to try each other's sugar sculptures. Although her sculpture became smaller, her heart filled with warmth.

At the Hexenzirkel stall, people could play three games at once, each featuring the witches Alice, Nicole, and Barbeloth. Nicole's game was Bing-Bang Finchball, while Alice's was Dodoco, where people blow up spiky fish warriors. Astrologer Barbeloth offered Columbina a fortune-telling with the Lunar Arcana before setting off on an unknown journey. Columbina had to choose four cards: a card of destiny, a card of the past, a card of the present, and a card of the future. As the Moon Goddess was about to draw the last card, it suddenly shifted, as if some force had influenced it. The first card was "The Moon," which can symbolize either truth or, conversely, deception. When the Moon is placed on the destiny tile, it indicates that the destiny is not what it may appear on the surface. Instead, it may yet have a hidden side. It symbolizes a journey through the fog, fraught with uncertainty and deception, where one must face inner challenges head-on. Columbina's second card was the inverted "Hermit." It symbolized isolation, truth out of reach, and a path that leads one astray. Combined with "The Moon" as one's destiny, "The Hermit" inverted represents a choice Columbina made to stand alone in the past. It was a choice made not out of fear or arrogance, but for reasons that others could not perceive. She fumbled through the darkness without a guide, unsure of her direction, and lost her way many times. The third card of the present was "The Lovers," signifying that the Moon Goddess had an unprecedented emotional experience, the joy of finding her soul becoming intertwined with that of another, a precious and beautiful encounter. But this card also symbolized an important decision and a parting of ways. And the final card of the future was "Death." This card could represent an agonizing death, a complete and utter end, or a rebirth. All four cards revealed that, in the past, Columbina may have lost her way, but now, she has gained new connections and new strength. She now faced an important decision that might bring about a great change in what is yet to come. This change would be either the end of all things or their beginning. Barbeloth warned that the presence of "The Moon" in her destiny could change absolutely everything, and she needed to see the truth clearly.

Since the party was filled with unusual activities, Alice invited the people of the fairytale land of Simulanka to join in. Paper squirrels and frogs played a floor game, while wooden figures, hamsters, and others participated in Dori's game, where people had to throw rings at them for points. Columbina managed to beat the previous record and won a Dodoco-Nicole toy. When Durin, who grew up in Simulanka, approached the Tale Ring Saga stall, his old acquaintances began to rush towards the rings, and Durin was able to win the grand prize, Dodoco-Alice. But to keep the children who wanted to play at the stall from getting upset, Columbina and Durin gave them their prizes.

Near the "Bitey the Frostfin Whale" stall, Columbina met her friend, the Fatui Harbinger, Sandrone. Although Sandrone denied coming to the party for Columbina, she didn't bring Pulonia and wore a cat-ear ornament. The game "Bitey the Frostfin Whale" required standing on certain "teeth" to prevent the Frostfin Whale's mouth from snapping shut. Because the Moon Goddess, using kuuvahki, sensed the safe teeth, she beat Sandrone twice. As they parted, the Moon Goddess promised to cherish the time they spent together and to miss her friend. Although Sandrone couldn't say it in person, she missed her too.

Near the game Bitey the Frostfin Whale, people gathered, battling their partners. As Columbina passed by, a girl dressed as the Moon Goddess challenged her to a duel. With her partner's help, Columbina was able to win the fight. Next to the arena was a stall selling Moon-Prayer Night candies. The Moon Goddess suggested that the vendor make new flavors, and then others joined in. Soon, Columbina received a whole box of candies with the flavors she'd ordered, which she wanted to share with her friends. Ashru got a mint candy, Sandrone got a coffee candy, Durin got an apple baked in shortcrust pastry, Albedo got a lemon candy, Paimon got a fruit candy, and the Traveler got a Smetana candy.

The stall of the Clink-Clank Krumkake Craftshop presented the game "Kuuhenki Concentration." Each player starts with differently colored kuuhenki, and each round, they draw one kuuhenki from their opponent. When a player has two kuuhenki of the same color, they make a pair and can be discarded, while those that can't form a pair must be kept. The round ends when a player can't form any more kuuhenki pairs, and that player gets a sticker. Aino, who was competing against Ineffa, was constantly losing and accused Ineffa of cheating. The Traveler, Paimon, and Columbina joined the game, and after a few rounds, they were all covered in stickers, but Ineffa still hadn't received a single one. Aino noticed how Ineffa not only remembered who had the Luonnotar, but every time someone drew a kuuhenki, she calculated and figured out all the probabilities of which kuuhenki would pair, who had which color kuuhenki, and even their facial expressions. Although Ineffa tried to deny cheating, the Traveler, Paimon, Columbina, and Aino pounced on her with stickers. Not far from Ineffa and Aino's stall, researcher Liouba was testing the robots' synchronization, and participants had to press a button at the right time and help the robot retrieve the treasure.

customize.name: Nod-Krai
customize.desc:
The moon-blessed land located in the northwestern regions of Teyvat.

Follow the silver thread spun by the new moon, traverse biting gales and desolate tundras as the snow-kissed lakes, fractured like mirrors, reflect their ageless, glacial radiance. The days are bitterly short, and the night stretches on like a dark, yawning maw. But even then, the light and song of the Welkin Moon will dance gently across the faces of visiting travelers. Up at ye towers, and let your lanterns blaze into the darkness! Until the day comes... when true moonlight bathes this land once more.

customize.name: Lempo Isle
customize.desc: An island where the border town, Nasha Town, is located. It is said that Nasha Town was first built by a group of children. Whenever they had a decision to make, they'd blow into a conch shell to gather the group, and everyone would vote on it.

customize.name: Simulanka
customize.desc:
A long, long time ago, three goddesses created this world and named it "Simulanka."

The Goddess of Creation, who presides over matter and magic, created the mountains and rivers and gave life. Her powers also paved the way for Simulanka to exist in numerous worlds.

After the Goddess of Creation came the Goddess of Prophecy, with dominion over the stars and the course of fate itself. She induced the sky to spin and the earth to move. Even to this day, her statue still stands tall at the highest point of Constellation Metropole.

The final Goddess was the Goddess of Fate, she who reigns over all treasured tales and dearest wishes. She bestowed the fierce and everlasting feelings of love and hate, and showed the meaning of death and hope.

customize.name: Frostmoon Scions
customize.desc: The descendants of the legendary golden realm, who chose to find new homes among the mountains and forests after abandoning all civilization. The only thing they never forsook was their faith in the "Moon Goddess."

customize.name: Moon Goddesses
customize.desc: Aria, Sonnet, and Canon — three sisters and Moon Goddesses who once ruled the firmament. Columbina Hyposelenia is a Moon Goddess who was born thousands of years after the Three Moon's death.

customize.name: Hexenzirkel
customize.desc: A secret witch society, which discusses secrets at the tea parties and explores Irminsul. There are eight witches in the Hexenzirkel.

customize.name: Lightkeepers
customize.desc: An ancient organization that has long defended Nod-Krai's freedom and peace against the ceaseless incursions and Wild Hunt attacks launched by the Abyss. The insignia of the Lightkeepers is a nightingale holding a burning wick in its beak.

customize.name: Curatorium of Secrets
customize.desc: A deep chasm filled with immense amounts of intelligence. They say that a northlands-spanning intel network lies behind this institution.

customize.name: Fatui
customize.desc: A Snezhnayan organization that is loyal to the Tsaritsa and has spread out all over the continent. Its Harbingers are on the hunt for the Gnoses.

customize.name: Columbina
customize.desc: The Trilune Goddess and the former Third of the Eleven Fatui Harbingers, known as Damselette. Her real name is Columbina Hyposelenia.

customize.name: Lauma
customize.desc: A Maiden blessed by moonlight and the grove alike, hope born to the Frostmoon Scions.

customize.name: Nefer
customize.desc: The remarkably resourceful owner of the Curatorium of Secrets.

customize.name: Jahoda
customize.desc: The Curatorium of Secrets' extremely reliable, do-it-all super employee (or so she claims).

customize.name: Sandrone
customize.desc: The Seventh of the Eleven Fatui Harbingers, known as Marionette.

customize.name: Ineffa
customize.desc: A multifunctional robot containing integrated mechanical components from various nations. The Source Core in her chest has endured the passage of countless years.

customize.name: Flins
customize.desc: A Lightkeeper of Nod-Krai, guardian of a lighthouse and graveyard on a northern isle. An enigmatic gentleman, cultured and courtly.

customize.name: Aino
customize.desc: A genius mechanic and inventor from Nod-Krai who loves interesting machines and sweet treats.

customize.name: Durin
customize.desc: A dragon born from M's pen, who came to alight in the human world. His "story" continues to unfold.

customize.name: Alice
customize.desc: The Sustainer of the World's Borders, Great Adventurer of the Realms, Dodo-King, Defender of Old Mondstadt, Friend of Adults Who Yet Harbor Hope, Author of the Teyvat Travel Guide, Originator of the Kujirai Art - Temari Jutsu, Supplier to the Renowned Lord Sangemah Bay, Elder and founder of the Hexenzirkel, Codename "A," Mother of Klee.

customize.name: Barbeloth
customize.desc: A visionary, a member of the Hexenzirkel, and Mona's teacher. She is also known as Astromancer Barbeloth Trismegistus and "B."

customize.name: Sugar Sculpture: Flins
customize.desc: A sugar sculpture crafted to capture a person's essence. The ancient, lonely lamp brings to mind Flins, standing guard by the graves.

customize.name: Sugar Sculpture: Kuuhenki
customize.desc: A sugar sculpture modeled after a mysterious creature. With an ethereal form, it's a kuuhenki drifting gently in the moonlight.

customize.name: Moon-Prayer Candy From Columbina
customize.desc: A Moon-Prayer Candy made by Columbina for everyone to enjoy. Inspired by her boundless imagination, this candy holds a wide variety of surprising flavors, perhaps drawn from the tastes she remembers most fondly.

customize.name: Moon-Prayer Night Pamphlet
customize.desc: A pamphlet handed out at Nasha Town's Moon-Prayer Night. It highlights a variety of fun booths and activities. With it in hand, guests are sure to enjoy an evening they won't soon forget.

customize.name: Lunar Arcana Case
customize.desc:
A card box given to you by a certain witch proficient in divination. It can be used to store the Lunar Arcana you find during your performances, cards which may also be exchanged with friends in Co-Op Mode.
Each world defines divination differently, but one thing remains constant — the use of "here" and "now" as anchors to unravel the unknown. Thus, the more Arcana one hoards within this box, the brighter the lantern of understanding burns...

value.name: Melting Moonlight in the Morning Mist
value.desc:
The Wild Hunt vanishes, chaos subsides, and the boughs of the Verdant Crest fill out quietly with life.

The Moon-Prayer Night, the night when the moon draws closest to Teyvat, is drawing near.

For a land and people long fractured, there is no better balm than a delightful night of celebration.

So why don't you and I step out together into this night of joy and laughter, amidst the blooming flowers bathed in the light of the moon?
